objective_text: You learn the structure and protocols of data networks used by computers and other end devices. You know the principles of planning a data network. You are familiar with protocols and data transmission principles used on the Internet. You know the layers of the OSI model and identify the technologies and protocols used on each layer. You can design a local area network using switches, routers, workstations, and servers. You are able to design cabling, switching topology, and routing scheme to run the data network. You know the different devices used on a network, such as switches, routers, firewalls, and wireless base stations. You can change, handle, and save the configuration used in network devices. You know how local area networks interconnect to one another through wide area networks.
competences_knowledge_text: You know the main modeling methods of data networks. You have knowledge and understanding of data networks and their effects. You know the basic principles of network design and how to configure network devices.
competences_practice_text: You can apply data network skills to communication between devices.
content_text: In this course, you will learn the principles of network structure and protocol design, as well as the principles of Internet communication. You will master the layers of the OSI model and be able to design and implement local area networks using switches, routers and servers. You will learn how to design cabling and routing plans and how to handle network equipment configurations. You will also understand how to efficiently connect local area networks to backbone networks. The contents stated through the OSI model: Layer 1: physical cabling (copper, fiber), wireless local area networks, basic modulations in data transfer, and devices. Layer 2: Ethernet switching, network segmentation (VLANs), loop detection (Spanning Tree), and MAC addressing. Layer 3: IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, subnetting, routing (Static, OSPF and BGP), DHCP, and ARP. Layer 4: TCP and UDP. Layers 5 to 7: SSH, HTTP, DNS, and SMTP. In addition, best practices in network design and configuration management are covered in the course.
prerequisites_text: Linux Basics
assessment_text:
Grade 1: The student knows the theory on network protocols sufficiently and is able to recognize some sections of existing solutions. The student can design and implement few parts of a small-scale network infrastructure based on given requirement specification.

objective_text: After completing the course, you will understand the most important concepts of the Linux operating system (Linux OS) and know how to work with and manage the operating system using a text-based user interface. After completing the course you can explain the key concepts of the Linux operating system and use basic commands and auxiliary programs given from the command line. You can manage the filesystem, user accounts and groups and understand the importance of access rights management. You can use package management systems to install and update software. You can monitor and manage system processes and services. You can solve common problems and troubleshoot using log files and network tools.
competences_knowledge_text: You understand the key concepts and architecture of the Linux operating system. You understand the importance of managing user accounts and groups.
competences_practice_text: You know how to manage the key functions of the Linux system and use command-line tools. You know how to manage the filesystem and user account permissions. You know how to install and update software and manage system processes and services.
content_text: In this course, you will learn how to effectively manage the Linux operating system using a text-based interface. You will understand key concepts and be able to use basic command line commands and utilities. You will learn how to manage the file system, user accounts and groups, and install and update software using package management systems. You will also be able to monitor system processes, solve common problems and troubleshoot using log files and network tools. Structure of filesystem. Basic commands of the filesystem. Access permissions. Auxiliary programs and tools. Package management. Process management. User management.
assessment_text:
Grade 1: You are familiar with the basic concepts of the Linux operating system and can use basic commands. You know how to create user groups, add users to them, and modify file and directory permissions at a basic level.
Grade 2: You understand the meaning of permissions and you are able to apply permissions in the management of filesystems. You know how to use simple command-line tools and auxiliary programs to perform tasks.
Grade 3: You know how to use groups to restrict access and manage user permissions. You understand the basics of package management and know how to install and update software. You know how to use various commands proficiently.
Grade 4: You know how to use groups to restrict access and manage user permissions effectively. You know how to use various commands proficiently. You understand the importance of process management and can manage active processes and services. You know how to schedule basic tasks using system tools.
Grade 5: You know how to comprehensively apply user groups and permission management, and combine various command-line tools to increase productivity. You know how to manage processes and various services comprehensively and effectively. You know how to schedule complex tasks using system tools. You know how to identify system problems using log files, documentation, and online resources.

You understand the need for managing containerized applications at scale and are familiar with orchestration tools, which help in deploying, scaling, and managing containerized applications. You understand concepts related to container networking and persistent storage, and can implement solutions in these areas within a containerized environment. You recognize the importance of security measures in container deployments.

Grade 3: You have a good understanding of the basic concepts of the servers and virtualization and know how to create your own virtual machines. You know how to effectively manage stacks of multiple containers and create container images tailored to specific needs.
Grade 4: You have a proficient understanding of the basic concepts of the servers and virtualization and know how to create your own virtual machines. You know how to excellently manage stacks of multiple containers and create container images tailored to specific needs.
Grade 5: You master the basic concepts of the servers and virtualization and know how to create your own virtual machines. You master how to manage stacks of multiple containers and create container images tailored to specific needs.

objective_text: In the course, you familiarise yourself with the basics of creating websites following good practices. After attending the course, you are able to define, plan and implement a standard and valid website, taking into account the target group using HTML and CSS technologies.
competences_knowledge_text: You know the web development process and its different stages as well as the definition of the target group.
competences_practice_text: You know the HTML5 standard and CSS style design and are able to create standard-compliant websites designed for the target group using basic techniques.
content_text: In this course, you will learn the basics and good practices of website design. By the end of the course, you will be able to define, design and implement a standard and valid website using HTML and CSS techniques, taking into account the needs of the target audience. You will be familiar with the different stages of the web development process and be able to apply HTML5 and CSS styling in practice. This course will enable you to create professional and targeted websites. Basics and documentation of website definition and design (e.g. synopsis, structure diagram, layout plan, testing, etc.). Website development process. Website Structure Syntax (HTML5). Designing the layout of the page with styles (CSS). Validation and accessibility considering different browsers. Publishing to the Internet on a web server.
prerequisites_text: ICT Skills
assessment_text:
Grade 1: You know Web standards and style design and how to produce a simple, valid and accessible website, taking the target group into account to some extent.
Grade 2: You understand Web standards and style design and can produce a valid and accessible website, taking the target group into account to some extent. The course assignment is documented but limited.
Grade 3: You know the HTML standard and style design and you know how to produce a valid and accessible website taking into account the target group. The course assignment is documented in accordance with the requirements.
Grade 4: You master the HTML standard and style design and know how to produce a functional, valid and accessible site, and for the most part, the target group has been taken into account. The documentation of the course assignment is thorough and error-free.
Grade 5: You have a comprehensive mastery of Web standards and style design and know how to produce an attractive (composition, graphics, colors, fonts, etc.), valid and accessible website, taking the target group into account in depth. The documentation of the course assignment is comprehensive, thorough, and error-free.

content_text: In this course, you will learn to understand the root causes of common web application security issues and use tools and methods to detect and exploit vulnerabilities in web applications. You will be able to provide remediation suggestions for identified risks. You will understand the basic methods related to web application security and their importance in analysis. We deal with various weaknesses related to web applications, such as identification of authentication, input validation, and configuration errors. We discuss the current trends in the cyber security environment and their effects on the network. OWASP TOP 10. Bug Bounty.

content_text: In this course, you will learn the principles, methods, and tools of software design. The primary goal is to strengthen your skills in requirements specification and service design, and to teach you how to document customer needs in a way that is useful for the product development team. You will learn to use the UML (Unified Modeling Language) and become familiar with common methods such as use case, sequence, state chart, and deployment diagrams. Additionally, you will learn to use MockUp tools to aid in requirements specification. During the course, you will learn to understand how software design is part of software production. You will identify the tasks related to the initial phase of the software life cycle, such as definition and analysis of software requirements, selection of the software implementation method and the impact of different interfaces on the design. You will also learn to document the design using common description methods. You will learn to use tools suitable for software design support. You will learn to consider different standards, good practices and ethical issues in design.

content_text: In this course, you will learn the mathematical foundations of 2D and 3D graphics programming, including vectors and matrices. objective_text: In the Graphics Programming Course, you learn the basics of real-time 3D graphics and programmable pipeline programming. The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of computer graphics, including how to develop and implement 3D graphics applications that are both visually appealing and interactive. Throughout the course, you learn about the key concepts of computer graphics, such as geometric transformations, shading models, and rasterization. You will also learn how to program graphics pipelines using modern, high-level graphics APIs such as OpenGL and Vulkan, and how to utilize modern graphics hardware to render 3D scenes in real-time. In addition, the course covers fundamental topics such as lighting, texturing, and object-oriented graphics programming, enabling you to develop complex, visually rich 3D applications. You also gain an understanding of how to use graphics frameworks and libraries to accelerate the development of your 3D graphics applications.
learning_outcomes_text: Throughout the course, you work on hands-on programming assignments, creating your own 3D graphics applications and learning to debug and optimize your code. By the end of the course, you have a deep understanding of real-time 3D graphics and the skills needed to develop and deploy high-performance graphics applications.

Additionally, you will gain an understanding of using graphics frameworks and libraries to accelerate your application development. The course covers modern graphics programming using OpenGL. objective_text: You learn to plan and implement Windows infrastructure according to the assignment as well as to monitor and maintain its functions and services. You also learn how to connect the environment to other information systems. You will learn to implement and plan a Windows environment in practice and understand its functions and services.
competences_knowledge_text: You understand the key features and architecture of a Windows server.
competences_practice_text: You know how to manage and configure services in the Windows environment. You know and are able to apply group policies in a Windows environment. You know how to connect Windows workstations to a Windows environment.
content_text: In this course, you will learn to design and implement a Windows infrastructure according to given requirements, as well as monitor and maintain its functions and services. You will also learn to integrate the environment with other information systems and understand the practical aspects of Windows environment functions and services. You will understand the key features and architecture of Windows servers and be able to manage and configure services within a Windows environment. The course equips you with the skills to apply group policies and connect Windows workstations to the Windows environment. Windows server basics, installation and configuration. Management and configuration of services. Management and utilisation of the Active Directory service. Management of group policies. Management of Windows workstations and information security. Basics of information security and best practices in Windows.
prerequisites_text: Windows Basics, Data Networks
assessment_text:
Grade 1: You know the basic features of a Windows server and have familiarized yourself with group policies. Your management and integration skills are limited.
Grade 2: You know how to deploy and configure a Windows server and manage simple group policies. You are able to integrate workstations at a basic level.
Grade 3: You manage the basic functions of a Windows server, you know more about managing group policies and smoothly integrate Windows workstations into a Windows environment.
Grade 4: You can effectively manage a more complex Windows environment. The in-depth management of group policies is smooth, and you have taken information security well into account.
Grade 5: You have excellent command of various aspects of the Windows environment, including complex group policies, service optimization, and environmental security.

content_text: In this course, you will learn the structure, protocols, and design principles of backbone networks. You will acquire the skills to seek information from industry standards and manuals to solve network issues in backbone networks. You will understand the protocols and data transmission principles in backbone networks and be able to configure the technologies and protocols used. The course equips you with the ability to design the necessary configurations for backbone networks and connect them to clients’ data center and local area networks, as well as other backbone networks. There are several technologies used in backbone networks and their development is continuous. The implementation of the course describes its current, essential technologies. This list described in the course description is indicative: Further details of the internal routing of the backbone network (Open Shortest Path First, Intermediate System to Intermediate System and Internal Border Gateway Protocol). More precise details of routing connecting backbone networks (External Border Gateway Protocol, BGP Metrics). Technologies that differentiate backbone customer traffic and speed up traffic control (LDP, MPLS-VPN, L2circuit, VPLS, Logical-systems, Routing-instances, Virtual Routing and Forwarding). Traffic prioritization of backbone networks (Quality of Service, DiffServ, DSCP). Traffic control of backbone networks (Traffic Engineering, Segment Routing).

There are several technologies used in backbone networks and their development is continuous. The implementation of the course describes its current, essential technologies. This list described in the course description is indicative: Further details of the internal routing of the backbone network (Open Shortest Path First, Intermediate System to Intermediate System and Internal Border Gateway Protocol). More precise details of routing connecting backbone networks (External Border Gateway Protocol, BGP Metrics). Technologies that differentiate backbone customer traffic and speed up traffic control (LDP, MPLS-VPN, L2circuit, VPLS, Logical-systems, Routing-instances, Virtual Routing and Forwarding). Traffic prioritization of backbone networks (Quality of Service, DiffServ, DSCP). Traffic control of backbone networks (Traffic Engineering, Segment Routing).
Prerequisites: Data networks, Servers and Containers, Local Area Networks

The student knows how to plan and implement parts of a small backbone network based on the specification of requirements.
Grade 2: The student satisfactorily masters the theory of backbone networks and identifies sections of existing backbone networks. The student can solve simple problems in backbone networks. The student knows how to plan and implement parts of a small backbone network based on the specification of requirements.
Grade 3: The student has a good command of the theory of backbone networks and recognizes sections of existing backbone networks. The student can solve problems with backbone networks. The student knows how to plan and implement parts of the backbone network based on the specification of requirements.
Grade 4: The student has a commendable command of the theory of backbone networks and recognizes sections of existing backbone networks. The student can solve problems with backbone networks. The student knows how to plan and implement parts of the backbone network based on the specification of requirements.
Grade 5: The student has an excellent command of the theory of backbone networks and comprehensively identifies sections of existing backbone networks. The student can solve complex problems with backbone networks. The student knows how to plan and implement a scalable backbone network based on requirements definition.

content_text: The course introduces the fundamentals of object-oriented programming concepts and object-oriented thinking and problem-solving using Python. Students learn to design coherent and reusable classes, model real-world domains, and implement various OOP programming techniques. Students practice computational thinking and systemic design by developing small-scale software applications and reasoning about program behavior through testing and refactoring. The course also integrates responsible AI-augmented development, where AI tools support exploration and testing while students maintain full responsibility for validation and correctness. 1. Foundations & Communication between Objects. Classes, objects, attributes, methods, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, class hierarchies, inter-object communication, and principles of coherent object design. 2. UML Diagrams. Using UML models such as class diagrams, sequence diagrams, and use case diagrams to support design, communication and documentation. 3. Software Development Process and Methods. Phases of software development: planning, implementation, testing, refactoring, clean code practices, and documentation for small-scale applications. Introduction to modular design and incremental improvement. 4. Principles AI augmented development. Responsive and responsible use of AI copilots to support code exploration, generate or refine test ideas, scaffold designs, and review code, combined with systematic human evaluation, validation, and interpretation of AI-produced suggestions.

content_text: The course focuses on designing and implementing mobile applications using modern programming practices, tools and frameworks. 1. Mobile Application Assignment. Planning and implementing a mobile application for an assigned task, using both manual and AI-assisted approaches for ideation and structure. 2. Mobile Programming Languages and Features. Exploring suitable programming languages, tools and mobile-specific features required for the application. 3. Design Patterns in Mobile Development. Learning and applying design patterns relevant to mobile applications, with AI-assisted examples to compare implementation alternatives. 4. Professional Development Tools. Using industry-standard coding tools, IDEs, version control systems and AI-supported tools for code generation, refactoring suggestions, debugging hints and documentation support. 5. Code Reuse and Framework Utilization. Reusing existing code and utilizing libraries, frameworks and platforms to accelerate development. Leveraging AI tools to explore documentation, assess library suitability and support integration tasks. 6. Team-Based Mobile Application Development. Developing a mobile application collaboratively in a team environment, practising structured workflows, shared coding practices and responsible AI use as part of teamwork and communication.
